BURHAN:v1p206/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p206/r1.speaker: عائشة
BURHAN:v1p206/r1.claim: The beginning-of-revelation report in al-Bukhari, explicitly authenticated by al-Hakim from Aisha, establishes اقرأ as the first revelation; Muslim gives it through “He taught man what he did not know.”
BURHAN:v1p206/r1.anchor: وأخرجه الحاكم فى مستدركه من حديث عائشة رضى الله عنها صريحا وقال صحيح الإسناد

BURHAN:v1p206/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p206/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p206/r2.claim: Muslim’s wording extends the first revelation through “He taught man what he did not know”; al-Bukhari’s version stops at “your Lord is most generous,” which the author calls an accepted abridgment.
BURHAN:v1p206/r2.anchor: ولفظ مسلم أول ما نزل من القرآن

ITQAN:v1p75/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p75/r1.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
ITQAN:v1p75/r1.claim: Ubayd b. ʿUmayr says Gabriel brought the Prophet a silk sheet and told him to recite; he identifies the opening of al-ʿAlaq as the first sura sent down.
ITQAN:v1p75/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن أشتة في كتاب المصاحف عن عبيد بن عمير قال جاء جبريل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بنمط فقال اقرأ

ITQAN:v1p75/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p75/r2.speaker: الزهري
ITQAN:v1p75/r2.claim: Al-Zuhrī recounts that while the Prophet was at Ḥirāʾ, an angel brought a silk sheet inscribed with the opening verses of al-ʿAlaq.
ITQAN:v1p75/r2.anchor: وأخرج عن الزهري أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء إذ أتى ملك بنمط من ديباج فيه مكتوب

BURSEVI:v10p364/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p364/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p364/r4.claim: The final clause specifies what God taught, by pen and directly: every kind of universal, particular, manifest, and hidden knowledge beyond prior imagination.
BURSEVI:v10p364/r4.anchor: بدل اشتمال من علم بالقلم وتعيين للمفعول أي علمه به

QASHANI:96:3-8/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:96:3-8/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:96:3-8/r3.claim: God taught the Prophet what he had not known and granted knowledge so that, before he was firmly established in abiding, he would not claim independent perfection and transgress through selfhood; self-sufficiency produces transgression.
QASHANI:96:3-8/r3.anchor: لم يكن له علم فعلمه بعلمه ووهب له صفة عالميته لئلا يرى ذاته موصوفة بصفة الكمال فيطغى

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r8.claim: God taught people what they did not know, including both necessary and acquired knowledge.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r8.anchor: علمهم ما لم يعلموا : الضروري ، والكسبي

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450/r2.claim: Qatada glosses what God taught people as writing.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450/r2.anchor: وفي قوله : علم الانسان ما لم يعلم قال الخط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.claim: Aisha narrates in the two Sahihs that Gabriel came to Muhammad in Hira, commanded him three times, embraced him forcefully each time, then recited the opening through 'what he did not know.'
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.anchor: وفي حديث ( الصحيحين ) عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قولها فيه : ( حتى جاءه الحق وهو في غار حراء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.claim: Aisha's narration is directly from the Prophet; her account that he returned trembling with the passage means he retained and recited what had been dictated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.anchor: فهذا الحديث روته عائشة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لقولها قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.claim: Khadija's request that Waraqa hear him further indicates Muhammad recited the revealed passage immediately; Gabriel's repeated command repeated God's wording to accustom him to reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.anchor: وهذا ينبىء بأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عندما قيل له بعد الفطة الثالثة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r2.claim: The clause is a new explanatory statement: Rabbuka is subject, with either 'who taught by the pen' or 'taught humanity what it did not know' as predicate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r2.anchor: و { ربك } مبتدأ وخبره إما { الذي علم بالقلم } وإما جملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r3.claim: Without Aisha's revelation report, the statement answers Muhammad's presumed question about reading without literacy: the one who taught writing can teach what he does not know.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r3.anchor: كيف أقرأ وأنا لا أحسن القراءة والكتابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r4.claim: With the hadith, the passage answers his 'I cannot read': God can teach by dictation, instruction, or inspiration, just as He taught Adam the names without literacy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r4.anchor: إذ العلم بالقراءة يحصل بوسائل أخرى مثل الإملاء والتلقين والإلهام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r6.claim: Al-Akram intensifies generosity rather than comparing God with another; generosity is giving benefit, and God's favors begin with creation and its sustaining provision.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r6.anchor: ووصف { الأكرم } مصوغ للدلالة على قوة الاتصاف بالكرم وليس مصوغا للمفاضلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.claim: The opening five verses gather divine attributes: lordship implies existence and oneness, creation and teaching indicate acts, and al-Akram entails perfection and freedom from deficiency.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.anchor: وقد جمعت هذه الآيات الخمس من أول السورة أصول الصفات الإلاهية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r6.claim: 'Taught humanity what it did not know' is the predicate of 'your Lord is most generous'; what comes between is parenthetical, and humanity is generic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p440/r6.anchor: وجملة : علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم } خبر عن قوله : { وربك الأكرم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r1.claim: Human learning comes by three routes: written transmission and reading across peoples and generations, oral teaching or dictation, and intellectual deductions and inventions; the latter two are included in God's broad teaching.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r1.anchor: الأخذ عن الغير بالمراجعة ، والمطالعة ، وطريقهما الكتابة وقراءة الكتب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r2.claim: This reassures the Prophet that illiteracy cannot prevent recitation: God can teach him without prior skill in writing, as He teaches all previously unknown things.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r2.anchor: وفي ذلك اطمئنان لنفس النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن عدم معرفته الكتابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r3.claim: The wording 'what he did not know' signals that knowledge follows a prior state of ignorance, so acquired learning is new to the learner.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r3.anchor: وأشعر قوله : { ما لم يعلم } أن العلم مسبوق بالجهل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r4.claim: The verse underscores the importance of writing and God's intention that the revelation be recorded; the Prophet therefore employed scribes from the start of his mission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r4.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى الاهتمام بعلم الكتابة وبأن الله يريد أن يكتب للنبيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r5.claim: The initial command and reference to pen teaching imply that Muhammad remained unlettered, an attribute completing the Qur'an's miracle, as another verse states.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r5.anchor: وفي الاقتصار على أمر الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بالقراءة ثم إخباره بأن الله علم الإنسان بالقلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.claim: These are the final five verses of the passage first revealed at Hira; the following discussion on verses 6–10 begins a new subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.anchor: وهذه آخر الخمس الآيات التي هي أول ما أنزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r4.claim: The human taught what he did not know may be Muhammad, but the generic human reading is stronger: God grants knowledge after ignorance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r4.anchor: قيل: المراد محمد عليه السلام، وقيل: اسم الجنس وهو الأظهر،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#3/r1.claim: The teaching includes writing, crafts and other knowledge that people did not previously know.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#3/r1.anchor: علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم من الخط والصنائع وغير ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#3/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes the human taught here to be Muhammad.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#3/r2.anchor: وقيل المراد بالإنسان هاهنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r1.claim: These first Qur'anic verses were the first mercy and blessing to people, reminding them of creation from a clot and God's generosity in teaching what people did not know.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r1.anchor: فأول شيء [نزل] (2) من القرآن هذه الآيات الكريمات المباركات (3) وهن أول رحمة رحم الله بها العباد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r2.claim: God honored humanity with knowledge, the distinction by which Adam surpassed the angels; knowledge exists mentally, verbally, and in writing, with writing entailing the other two but not vice versa, hence the mention of the pen.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r2.anchor: وفيها التنبيه على ابتداء خلق الإنسان من علقة، وأن من كرمه تعالى أن علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم، فشرفه وكرمه بالعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r4.claim: Another maxim says whoever acts on what he knows will be granted knowledge of what he did not know.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437/r4.anchor: وفيه أيضا: "من عمل بما علم رزقه (5) الله علم ما لم يكن [يعلم] (6)

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan and has seventeen verses.

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.speaker: عائشة ومجاهد وعطاء بن يسار
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.claim: One report says the first revelation from the Qur'an was Iqraʾ bismi rabbik.
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.anchor: قيل: أول ما نزل من القرآن: (اقرأ باسم ربك)، عن عائشة، ومجاهد، وعطاء بن يسار.

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.claim: Another report says the first five verses descended first, while the rest of the surah came later; a similar report is attributed to ʿĀʾisha.
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.anchor: وقيل: أول ما نزل منها خمس آيات إلى قوله: (ما لم يعلم)، ثم نزل باقي السورة بعد ذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r7.claim: Teaching writing and what people did not know is the highest sign of God's generosity, moving humanity from ignorance to knowledge.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r7.anchor: حيث قال : الأكرم { الذي علم بالقلم * علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم }

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r19.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r19.claim: One explanation of what humanity did not know is writing with the pen.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r19.anchor: أحدهما : الخط بالقلم , قاله قتادة وابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r20.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r20.claim: Another explanation is that God taught people every craft they learned.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r20.anchor: الثاني : علمه كل صنعة علمها فتعلم , قاله ابن شجرة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r21.claim: A further possibility is that God taught humanity about its initial creation as evidence of its Creator, who later moves it as He wills.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r21.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : علمه من حاله في ابتداء خلقه ما يستدل به على خلقه وأن ينقله من بعد على إرادته .

MUQATIL:96:1-8/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:96:1-8/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:96:1-8/r3.claim: The pen passage means God taught writing and taught the human being the Qur'an, knowledge previously unknown.

MUQATIL:96:1-8/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:96:1-8/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:96:1-8/r7.claim: The revelation of God teaching the human what he did not know came while the Prophet was at al-Arāk in the forenoon.
MUQATIL:96:1-8/r7.anchor: والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يومئذ بالأراك ضحى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#8/r1.claim: God's teaching humanity what it did not know demonstrates His generosity, transfers people from ignorance to knowledge, and highlights the benefit of writing, which preserves learning, wisdom, and ancient reports.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#8/r1.anchor: فدل على كمال كرمه بأنه علم عباده ما لم يعلموا ونقلهم من ظلمة الجهل إلى نور العلم

QURTUBI-FULL:96:5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:5/r1.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:96:5/r1.claim: One view identifies the human as Adam, taught the names of all things in al-Baqara; Adam recited them to the angels, displaying his rank, establishing his prophethood and God's proof, after which his descendants inherited and transmitted knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:5/r1.anchor: قيل: «الإنسان» هنا آدم عليه السلام. علمه أسماء كل شيء حسب ما جاء به القرآن

QURTUBI-FULL:96:5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:5/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:96:5/r2.claim: Another view identifies the human as Muhammad, based on the statement that God taught him what he had not known; on this reading teaching is future because this was among the earliest revelations.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:5/r2.anchor: وقيل: «الإنسان» هنا الرسول محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم دليله قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:96:5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:5/r3.claim: A general interpretation covers humanity, since God brings people from their mothers knowing nothing.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:5/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو عام لقوله تعالى: والله أخرجكم من بطون أمهاتكم لا تعلمون شيئا

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r1.claim: God is the source of all human learning and every discovery about existence, life, and the self; all knowledge comes from this one source.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r1.anchor: إن مصدره هو الله . منه يستمد الإنسان كل ما علم ، وكل ما يعلم

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r2.claim: The opening revelation establishes a broad faith principle: every affair, movement, step, and deed begins in God's name, proceeds in His name, and returns to Him.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r2.anchor: كل أمر . كل حركة . كل خطوة . كل عمل . باسم الله

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r3.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r3.claim: Qutb cites Ibn al-Qayyim's summary that the Prophet remembered God in speech, commands, rulings, reports, praise, prayer, silence, and every circumstance.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r3.anchor: قال الإمام شمس الدين أبو عبد الله محمد بن قيم الجوزية في كتابه

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r4.claim: The Prophet praised God upon waking for reviving him after sleep and affirmed that resurrection returns to Him.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r4.anchor: وكان إذا استيقظ قال : الحمد لله الذي أحيانا بعد ما أماتنا

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r5.speaker: عائشة
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r5.claim: Aisha reports that when the Prophet awoke at night, he magnified and professed God's oneness ten times, then sought refuge from the constriction of this life and Judgment before beginning prayer.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r5.anchor: وقالت عائشة كان إذا هب من الليل كبر عشرا ، وهلّل عشرا

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r6.speaker: عائشة
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r6.claim: Aisha also reports his waking supplication seeking forgiveness, mercy, increased knowledge, a steadfast heart, and a gift of divine mercy.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r6.anchor: وقالت أيضا : كان إذا استيقظ من الليل قال : لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r7.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r7.claim: A report says that whoever wakes at night and remembers God, praises Him, and asks forgiveness or makes another supplication receives an answer; if he then performs ablution and prays, the prayer is accepted. Qutb cites Bukhari.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r7.anchor: وأخبر أن من استيقظ من الليل فقال

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r8.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet woke at night while staying with him, recited the closing verses of Al Imran, then prayed with praise affirming God's sovereignty, truth, revelation, resurrection, and the articles of faith.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس عنه [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] ليلة مبيته عنده

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r9.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r9.speaker: عائشة
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r9.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet sometimes began night prayer by asking the Lord of Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil to guide him to the truth in disputed matters.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r9.anchor: وقد قالت عائشة - رضي الله عنها - كان إذا قام من الليل قال

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r10.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r10.claim: After finishing Witr, the Prophet ended it by saying “Subbuh, Quddus” three times, lengthening his voice on the third repetition.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r10.anchor: وكان إذا أوتر ختم وتره بعد فراغه بقوله : سبحان الله القدوس

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r11.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r11.claim: On leaving home, the Prophet asked God's protection from straying or misleading, slipping, injustice, and ignorance; Qutb labels this report sound.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r11.anchor: وكان إذا خرج من بيته يقول : بسم الله توكلت على الله

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r12.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r12.claim: The Prophet taught that one who leaves home saying God's name, trusting Him, and acknowledging there is no power except through Him is guided, protected, and spared Satan; Qutb grades the report good.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r12.anchor: وقال [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] من قال إذا خرج من بيته

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r13.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet left for dawn prayer asking God to place light in his heart, tongue, hearing, sight, and all directions, and to increase his light.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r13.anchor: وقال ابن عباس عنه - ليلة مبيته عنده - : إنه خرج إلى صلاة الفجر

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r14.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r14.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r14.claim: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reports a supplication for going to prayer without pride, show, or malice, asking forgiveness and refuge from Hell; God appoints seventy thousand angels to seek forgiveness for the worshipper.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r14.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري : قال : قال رسول الله

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r15.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r15.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r15.claim: When entering a mosque, the Prophet sought God's protection from Satan; Qutb reports that Satan then says the person is protected from him for the rest of the day.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r15.anchor: وذكر أبو داود عنه [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أنه كان إذا دخل المسجد

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r16.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r16.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r16.claim: The Prophet taught worshippers entering the mosque to pray for blessings on him and ask God to open mercy's doors, then on leaving to ask for His bounty; another report adds forgiveness and the doors of mercy or bounty.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r16.anchor: إذا دخل أحدكم المسجد فليصل وليسلم على النبي [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] وليقل

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r17.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r17.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r17.claim: The Prophet used to remain in his prayer place after dawn until sunrise remembering God; he taught morning and evening remembrances. Qutb calls one report sound and cites Muslim for another.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r17.anchor: وكان إذا صلى الصبح جلس في مصلاه حتى تطلع الشمس يذكر الله

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r18.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r18.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r18.claim: At Abu Bakr's request for morning, evening, and bedtime words, the Prophet taught a prayer seeking refuge from one's own evil, Satan, and causing harm to oneself or another Muslim; Qutb calls it sound.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r18.anchor: وقال له أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه - مرني بكلمات أقولهن إذا أصبحت وإذا أمسيت

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r19.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r19.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r19.claim: When putting on a new garment, the Prophet named it and praised God for clothing him, asking for its good and protection from its harm; Qutb calls the report sound.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r19.anchor: وكان [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] إذا استجد ثوبا سماه باسمه عمامة أو قميصا

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r20.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r20.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r20.claim: When returning home, the Prophet praised God for shelter, food, drink, and favor, and asked to be protected from the Fire.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r20.anchor: ويذكر عنه [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أنه كان يقول إذا انقلب إلى بيته

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r21.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r21.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r21.claim: In the two Sahih collections, the Prophet's supplication upon entering the lavatory seeks refuge from impure male and female devils.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r21.anchor: وثبت عنه في الصحيحين أنه كان يقول عند دخوله الخلاء

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r22.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r22.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r22.claim: The Prophet said “Your forgiveness” after leaving the lavatory; another report, cited from Ibn Majah, praises God for removing harm and granting health.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r22.anchor: وكان إذا خرج من الخلاء قال :

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r23.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r23.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r23.claim: The Prophet put his hand in a water vessel and told the Companions to perform ablution in God's name.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r23.anchor: وثبت عنه أنه وضع يده في الإناء الذي فيه الماء ، ثم قال للصحابة

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r24.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r24.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r24.claim: When seeing the new moon, the Prophet asked God to bring it with security, faith, safety, and Islam; Qutb cites al-Tirmidhi grading this report good.

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r25.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r25.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r25.claim: The Prophet instructed diners to say God's name before eating and, if they forgot, to say it at the beginning and end; Qutb calls the report sound.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r25.anchor: وكان إذا وضع يده في الطعام قال : باسم الله . ويأمر الآكل بالتسمية

QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r26.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r26.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r26.claim: The Prophet's entire life, down to its smallest details, was shaped by the divine instruction received at the first revelation and by its foundational faith conception.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:5/r26.anchor: وهكذا كانت حياته كلها [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] بدقائقها متأثرة بهذا التوجيه الإلهي

RAZI-FULL:v32p18/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p18/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p18/r1.claim: The phrase may refer to God's teaching by pen and also to other instruction, with a conjunction omitted; or both clauses may mean that the pen taught humanity what it did not know, the second explaining the first.
RAZI-FULL:v32p18/r1.anchor: فيحتمل أن يكون المراد علمه بالقلم وعلمه أيضا غير ذلك ولم يذكر واو النسق

SAMIN-DURR:96:4-5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:4-5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:4-5/r1.claim: The phrase about teaching by the pen and teaching humanity resembles create/create humanity, so the same grammatical analyses apply.
SAMIN-DURR:96:4-5/r1.anchor: قريب من قوله: " خلق، خلق الإنسان " فلك أن تعيد فيه ما تقدم

STUDYQURAN:96:1/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:96:1/r9.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:96:1/r9.claim: Some take “man” as Adam, taught all the names; others as Muhammad, taught the Book and Wisdom; most commentators take it to mean all humanity.
STUDYQURAN:96:1/r9.anchor: But here most commentators take taught man to mean that this verse refers to the manner in which God teaches all human beings

TAB:96:3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r4.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r4.claim: Aisha recounts true dreams, Muhammad's retreat at Hira, Gabriel's arrival and repeated command to read, and identifies these opening verses as the first revelation.
TAB:96:3/r4.anchor: عن عائشة أنها قالت :  كان أوّل ما ابتدىء به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة

TAB:96:3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r5.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r5.claim: In Aisha's report, Khadija reassures Muhammad by citing his virtues; Waraqa identifies the revelation as Moses' angel, predicts opposition, and vows support if alive.
TAB:96:3/r5.anchor: فَقَالَتْ :  أبْشِرْ ،   فَوَاللّهِ لا يُخْزيكَ اللّهُ أبَدا ،   وَوَاللّهِ إنّكَ لَتَصِلُ الرّحَمِ

TAB:96:3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r6.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r6.claim: Aisha's account says that after Iqra the next revelations included Nun, the Pen, al-Muddaththir, and al-Duha.
TAB:96:3/r6.anchor: ثُمّ كانَ أوّلُ ما نَزَلَ عَليّ مِنَ القُرآنِ بَعْدَ «اقْرأْ » :  ( ن والقَلَمِ وَما يَسْطُرُونَ

TAB:96:3/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
TAB:96:3/r7.claim: Ibn Shaddad reports Gabriel's reading of the opening passage, Khadija's reassurance and referral to Waraqa, then delayed revelation and al-Duha's reassurance.
TAB:96:3/r7.anchor: حدثنا عبد الله بن شدّاد ،   قال :  أتى جبريل محمدا ،   فقال :  يا محمد اقرأ

TAB:96:3/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r8.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r8.claim: Aisha, through ʿUrwa and al-Zuhri, is cited as saying the first thing revealed was ‘Read in the name of your Lord who created.’
TAB:96:3/r8.anchor: عن عائشة قال إبراهيم :  قال سفيان :  حفظه لنا ابن إسحاق :  إن أوّل شيء أُنزل من القرآن :  اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r9.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r9.claim: A further report from Aisha says the first surah revealed was Iqra bi-smi rabbika.
TAB:96:3/r9.anchor: عن عائشة ،   أنّ أوّل سورة أُنزلت من القرآن اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r10.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
TAB:96:3/r10.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr says the first surah sent down to the Messenger was Iqra bi-smi rabbika alladhi khalaq.
TAB:96:3/r10.anchor: عن عُبيد بن عُمير ،   قال :  أوّل سورة نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اقرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r11.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
TAB:96:3/r11.claim: Abu Raja says he learned Iqra from Abu Musa al-Ashʿari and identifies it as Muhammad's first revealed surah.
TAB:96:3/r11.anchor: أبو رجاء العُطارديّ ،   قال :  كنا في المسجد الجامع ،   ومقرئنا أبو موسى الأشعريّ

TAB:96:3/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r12.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
TAB:96:3/r12.claim: ʿAta ibn Yasar says Iqra was the first surah revealed from the Qur'an.
TAB:96:3/r12.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار ،   قال :  أوّل سورة نزلت من القرآن اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r13.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:96:3/r13.claim: Mujahid says Iqra was the first Qur'anic revelation; one transmission adds that Nun and the Pen followed.
TAB:96:3/r13.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قال :  أوّل ما نزل من القرآن :  اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ وزاد ابن مهديّ :  ن والْقَلَمِ
