TAB-FULL:v24p530/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p530/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
TAB-FULL:v24p530/r1.claim: A report says Gabriel commanded Muḥammad to read through the verse about teaching what was unknown; he feared something had happened, Khadīja reassured him, and later the pause in revelation led to the opening verses of Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā.
TAB-FULL:v24p530/r1.anchor: قال: ثنا عبد الله بن شداد، قال: أتى جبريل محمدا، فقال: يا محمد اقرأ، فقال: «وما أقرأ؟»

TAB-FULL:v24p532/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p532/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p532/r1.claim: God taught people writing with the pen, along with other things they did not know.
TAB-FULL:v24p532/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم} [العلق: 5] قال: علم الإنسان خطا بالقلم

TAB-FULL:v24p532/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p532/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p532/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd specifically glosses the teaching as teaching people to write with the pen.
TAB-FULL:v24p532/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم} [العلق: 5] قال: علم الإنسان خطا بالقلم

TABATABAI:96:1-7/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r12.claim: The statement that God taught people what they did not know generalizes the blessing and further reassures the Prophet.
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r12.anchor: ثم عمم سبحانه النعمة فذكر تعليمه للإنسان ما لم يعلم

TABATABAI:96:1-7/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r13.anchor: والمراد بالإنسان الجنس كما هو ظاهر السياق

TABATABAI:96:1-7/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r14.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r14.claim: Alternative identifications of humankind are Adam, Idris as the first to write, or every prophet who wrote; the author regards them as weak and unnatural.
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r14.anchor: وقيل المراد به آدم عليه السلام، وقيل إدريس عليه السلام لأنه أول من خط بالقلم

TABATABAI:96:1-7/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r15.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r15.claim: A further interpretation identifies humankind as every prophet who wrote; the author considers this and the preceding proposals remote.
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r15.anchor: وقيل كل نبي كان يكتب وهي وجوه ضعيفة بعيدة عن الفهم

TABRISI:96:3-10/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:3-10/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:3-10/r10.claim: God taught people guidance, expression, religion, laws, and rulings; human knowledge comes through intuition, rational evidence, or teaching by angels and messengers, so all knowledge is attributable to Him. This indicates that God is knowing, since knowledge comes only from a knower.
TABRISI:96:3-10/r10.anchor: من أنواع الهدى والبيان وأمور الدين والشرائع والأحكام فجميع ما يعلمه الإنسان من جهته سبحانه

THALABI:v10p245/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p245/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p245/r1.claim: God taught people forms of guidance, explanation, and action that they did not know.
THALABI:v10p245/r1.anchor: علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم من البيان والعمل

THALABI:v10p245/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p245/r2.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p245/r2.claim: Knowledge is God’s blessing: without it religion would not stand and livelihood would not be sound.
THALABI:v10p245/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: العلم نعمة من الله، لولا العلم لم يقم دين ولم يصلح عيش

THALABI:v10p245/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p245/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p245/r3.claim: Another view says the human taught was Adam, whom God taught all the names.

THALABI:v10p245/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p245/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p245/r4.claim: Another view identifies the human as Muḥammad and links the verse to God’s teaching him what he had not known.
THALABI:v10p245/r4.anchor: وقيل: الإنسان هاهنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، بيانه وعلمك ما لم تكن

ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n3/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n3/r1.claim: The pen symbolizes writing and recorded knowledge, clarifying the summons to read; writing carries ideas and experience across people, generations, and cultures, making human knowledge cumulative and giving each person access to what they could not know alone.
ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n3/r1.anchor: "The pen" is used here as a symbol for the art of writing or

ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n3/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n3/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n3/r2.claim: God's teaching also means revelation through prophets of spiritual truths and moral standards that human experience and reasoning alone cannot establish unequivocally.
ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n3/r2.anchor: God's "teaching" man signifies also the act of His revealing, through the prophets

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p170#4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p170#4/r1.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p170#4/r1.claim: The object of “taught by the pen” is omitted and supplied by verse 5: God taught humans through the pen what they did not know; repeating “taught” emphasizes it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p170#4/r1.anchor: وقال صاحب النظم: مفعول قوله: {علم بالقلم} محذوف، فلما ذكر قوله: {علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم} انتظم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p170#4/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p170#4/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p170#4/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī likewise understands the knowledge in verse 5 as writing in a book by means of the pen.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p170#4/r2.anchor: وهذا معنى قول الكلبي؛ (لأنه قال) (¬8): {علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم} من الكتاب بالقلم.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p170#4/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p170#4/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p170#4/r3.claim: Some commentators detach verse 5 from the prior one and say God taught Adam all the names.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p170#4/r3.anchor: ومن المفسرين من يجعل هذه الآية منقطعة عن الأولى فيقول: معنى {علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم} علم آدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p170#4/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p170#4/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p170#4/r4.claim: Another view says God taught Muḥammad previously unknown rulings, religious law, and prophetic stories, citing 4:113; the author calls it weak because this was among the first revelations and Muḥammad then knew little.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p170#4/r4.anchor: ومنهم من يقول: علم محمدا ما لم يعلم من الأحكام والشريعة، وقصص النبيين كما قال: {وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم}

WAHIDI-QT:96:4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:4/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:4/r1.claim: God taught by the pen, explaining His teaching as handwriting and writing.
WAHIDI-QT:96:4/r1.anchor: { الذي علم بالقلم } ثم بين ما علم فقال { علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم } وهو الخط والكتابة

WAHIDI-QT:96:5/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:5/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:5/r1.claim: The knowledge God taught humanity includes handwriting and writing.
WAHIDI-QT:96:5/r1.anchor: { الذي علم بالقلم } ثم بين ما علم فقال { علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم } وهو الخط والكتابة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r6.claim: God taught humanity what it had not known, namely script and writing.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r6.anchor: علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم } وهو الخط والكتابة.

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r16.claim: God teaches the unknown by creating capacities and faculties, setting up proofs and sending signs and revelations, through both gifted and acquired learning.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r16.anchor: insanda olmayan kuvveleri, isti‘dadları, melekeleri yaratarak ve deliller nasb u ikāme ederek ve âyetler inzal eyleyerek vehbî olarak da öğretti, kesbî olarak da öğretti

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r17.speaker: Beyzâvî
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r17.claim: Beyzawi says God recounts the human's beginning and end while moving him from the lowest state to the highest, first indicating rational knowledge of God and then signifying transmitted knowledge.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r17.anchor: Beyzâvî der ki: “Allah sübhânehu insanı ehass-ı merâtibden

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r2.claim: It is significant that the first revealed verses unite rational and transmitted proof and present recitation, writing, and knowledge as great divine gifts; the pen also encourages the community to literacy.

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r4.claim: The Prophet never wrote with his own hand and needed no writing to retain revelation because God promised he would not forget in 87:6; he recited and dictated the revelation to scribes for the community.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r4.anchor: hıfz u zabt için de yazmaya ihtiyâcı olmadığı, fakat nâzil olanı ümmetin hıfzı için vahiy kâtiblerine okuyup yazdırdığı mâlumdur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r1.claim: These were the first revelation; the command to read addresses Muhammad and all Muslims, and its repetition stresses the importance of reading and knowledge, through which humans are distinguished among living things.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r1.anchor: İlk vahyin “oku” emriyle başlaması ve bu emrin iki defa tekrar edilmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r7.claim: The pen preserves and transmits sciences, wisdom, history, books, and revelation across generations; its functional sense includes all tools of reading, writing, and information exchange through computers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r7.anchor: bilinen kalemden bilgisayara kadar bütün okuma, yazma ve bilgi alıp verme araçlarını kapsadığını

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p387/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p387/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p387/r3.claim: The teaching of what was unknown is primarily the favor given to the unlettered Arab first audience: complete guidance led them from ignorance, and they must honor it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p387/r3.anchor: the unlettered Arabs were not only bestowed with divine guidance in written form

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p387/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p387/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p387/r4.claim: The sūrah al-Jumu‘ah passage also describes God sending a prophet among the unlettered who recites revelation and teaches the Book and wisdom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p387/r4.anchor: It is He Who has sent forth among the unlettered a prophet from among

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r1.speaker: some people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p392/r1.claim: One reported view makes the whole of Sūrah al-‘Alaq the Qur’an’s first revelation; the majority instead regards its first five verses as first, based on a report in Bukhārī and Muslim.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r13.claim: Al-insān is generic here, and God recounts humanity's acquisition of sciences after prior ignorance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r13.anchor: والإنسان في قوله: علم الإنسان، الظاهر أنه اسم الجنس. عدد عليه اكتساب العلوم بعد الجهل بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r1.claim: An alternative identifies the human taught in the preceding verse as the Messenger.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r1.claim: The clause is an explanatory substitution for teaching by the pen: God teaches humans with and without writing all kinds of knowledge they had not imagined; the omitted first object and explicit lack of prior knowledge stress divine power and generosity and the Prophet's vast learning.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r1.anchor: بدل اشتمال من علم بالقلم أي علمه به وبدونه من الأمور الكلية والجزئية والجلية ما لم يخطر بباله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r2.speaker: ابن الزبير
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r2.claim: Some supply script as the object of taught, supported by Ibn al-Zubayr's reading الذي علم الخط بالقلم.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r2.anchor: وقدر بعضهم مفعول علم الخط وجعل بالقلم متعلقا به وأيد بقراءة ابن الزبير الذي علم الخط بالقلم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r4.claim: If the reading is for proclamation, the command means to tell one's people that the generous Lord rewards work, strengthens the Prophet to retain the Quran, and enables its delivery.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r4.anchor: وحاصل المعنى على إرادة القراءة للتبليغ في قول بلغ قومك وربك الأكرم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r7.speaker: الضحاك، كعب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r7.claim: The verse does not identify the teacher; reports say every prophet who wrote, or name Idris and Adam as the first writers. Al-Alusi doubts claims that they invented particular alphabets.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r7.anchor: وقيل هو كل نبي كتب وقال الضحاك هو إدويس عليه السلام وهو أول من خط وقال كعب هو آدم عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r8.claim: The passage praises writing’s benefits and high status: without it religion would not stand and life would not be sound; the pen and script alone suffice as a sign of God’s subtle wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180#4/r8.anchor: وقد أدمج سبحانه وتعالى التنبيه على فضل علم الكتابة لما فيه من المنافع العظيمة ونيل الرتب الفخيمة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r1.claim: Writing was ancient among non-Arab peoples but a later arrival among Arabs, especially in the Hijaz, according to the apparent historical reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r1.anchor: وظاهر الآثار أن الكتابة في الأمم غير العرب قديمة وفيهم حادثة لا سيما في أهل الحجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r2.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r2.claim: The continuation of a pen poem uses an image of a jinn and eager hands around the writing tool to evoke the power of writing.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r3.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r3.claim: Another poem that al-Zamakhshari attributes to an unnamed poet praises calligraphic pens and the far reach of writing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r3.anchor: ومما نسبه الزمخشري في ذلك لبعضهم وعنى على ما قيل نفسه ورواقم رقش كمثل أراقم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r4.speaker: الكلبي، الهيثم بن عدي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi and al-Haytham ibn Adi report that writing was ancient among non-Arabs but newly acquired in the Hijaz, transferred from Hira by Harb ibn Umayya after he learned it in the region of al-Anbar; the chain of reported teachers leads through Aslam ibn Sidra to Maramir ibn Murra.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r4.anchor: وأنهم أخذوا من أهل الأنبار وذكر الكلبي والهيثم بن عدي أن الناقل للخط العربي من العراق إلى الحجاز حرب ابن أمية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r5.claim: Himyar reportedly used the separate, unjoined Musnad script, taught only with permission; one claim counts twelve major script families, which al-Alusi allows only if these are origins since derivative scripts are too many to count.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p181/r5.anchor: وكان لها شأن عندهم فلا يتعاطاها إلا من إذن له تعلمها وأصناف الكتابة كثيرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r1.claim: Most commentators say this was the first sura revealed and that its first five verses, through the words about what humanity did not know, were the first revelation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r1.anchor: أكثر المفسرين: على أن هذه السورة أول سورة نزلت من القرآن، وأول ما نزل خمس آيات من أولها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r2.claim: God taught humanity kinds of guidance and clear expression.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r2.anchor: علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم} من أنواع الهدى والبيان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r3.claim: Another interpretation says God taught Adam all the names.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes the human to be Muhammad, citing 4:113.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: الإنسان هاهنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بيانه: "وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم" (النساء -113)

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r2.claim: God teaches through created faculties, established signs, and revealed verses, including teaching reading to one who could not read.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r2.anchor: بخلق القوى ونصب الدلائل وإنزال الآيات فيعلمك القراءة وإن لم تكن قارئا

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r3.claim: God recounts humanity's beginning and destination to show the favor of raising it from the lowest rank to the highest, affirm His lordship and generosity, and move from rational proof to sensory evidence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r3.anchor: وقد عدد سبحانه وتعالى مبدأ أمر الإنسان ومنتهاه إظهارا لما أنعم عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.claim: A report promises the reciter a reward as though he had recited the entire set of shorter suras.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

BINTSHATI:v2p13/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r2.claim: She presents the surah’s opening as the first revelation, noting that Ibn Ishaq and al-Tabari report no disagreement about that account.
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r2.anchor: والمشهور كذلك أنه أمل سورة نزلت من الوحي. ولم يشر "ابن إسحاق" في (السيرة النبوية) إلي خلاف

BINTSHATI:v2p13/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r3.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r3.claim: Aisha recounts Muhammad’s true dreams, retreat to Hira, Gabriel’s command and three embraces, and the recitation of the opening five verses, which remained fixed in his heart; no grading is stated.
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r3.anchor: عن "السيدة عائشة أم المؤمنين" قالت: "كان أول ما ابتدئ به رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من الوحي

BINTSHATI:v2p13/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r4.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r4.claim: Aisha continues that Muhammad saw Gabriel in the sky, returned to Khadija, and was reassured because his character included kinship, truthfulness, trustworthiness, hospitality, and helping in adversity; no grading is stated.
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r4.anchor: فقالت: أبشر يا ابن عم واثبت، فوالله لا يخزيك الله أبداً، إنك لتصل الرحم وتصدق الحديث

BINTSHATI:v2p14/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r3.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r3.claim: Al-Razi also transmits that only al-Alaq’s first five verses came at the start; the remainder came after public opposition and were joined to the surah by God’s command.
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r3.anchor: أن الذي نزل من السورة أول الوحي، آياتها الخمس الأولى

BINTSHATI:v2p14/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r4.claim: Al-Bahr al-Muhit says the surah is Meccan and its opening was the first revelation at Hira, as established in Bukhari and elsewhere; it judges the claims that al-Muddaththir or the Fatiha came first unsound.
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r4.anchor: وقول جابر: أول ما نزل المدثر، وقول أبي ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل: أول ما نزل الفاتحة، لا يصح

BINTSHATI:v2p15/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r1.claim: The reports in al-Tabari and the Prophetic biography stop the first-revelation account at verse five, supporting the view that the opening alone was first revealed.
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r1.anchor: حيث يقف الحديث فيهما عن اول ما نزل من الوحي، عند الآية الخامسة

BINTSHATI:v2p24/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r1.claim: Some exegetes limit the taught human to Idris or Adam, the first to write with a pen; the author rejects this restriction in favor of the generic human.
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r1.anchor: ومن المفسرين من قدر في الآية علمه الله، قيل: هو" إدريس، وقيل آدم لأنه أول من كتب بالقلم"

BINTSHATI:v2p24/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r2.claim: Human is an unrestricted species term: God taught humanity all acquired knowledge, without need to specify which knowledge or limit it to a single person.
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r2.anchor: بل هو الإنسان، اسماً لعموم الجنس على إطلاقه، علمه الله ما لم يعلم

BINTSHATI:v2p24/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to gloss the verse as teaching writing by the pen; Abu Hayyan judges this to be an explanatory reading.
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r3.anchor: ما روى عن "ابن عباس" من أنه قرأ الآية: "علم الخط بالقلم"

BINTSHATI:v2p24/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r4.claim: The warning turns to the human tendency to become arrogant about knowledge and status among created beings.
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r4.anchor: ويمضي البيان القرآني، في الردع المحذر مما يتعرض له الإنسان من غرور بعلمه ومكانه بين المحلوقات

BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r2.claim: God teaches necessary and theoretical knowledge, including scripture, religious practice, transactions, and crafts, while also giving uncaused insight into reasoning, conclusions, and intuitive truths.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r2.anchor: أي الذي من شأنه الأنس بما هو فيه لا ينتقل إلى غيره بل ينساه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r3.claim: If learning came only through ordinary causes, people would be equal in teaching time and basic knowledge as they are in gestation and humanity; divine bestowal accounts for their differences.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r3.anchor: ولو كان ذلك بالأسباب فقط لتساوى الناس في مدة التعليم وفي أصل المعلوم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r6.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī remarks that each of the two worlds, creation and command, has both a particular and a universal aspect.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r6.anchor: قال الرازي , وفي كل من العالمين خصوص وعموم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r7.claim: God teaches the unlettered Prophet, making him more learned than those who write and raising him above every lofty station.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r7.anchor: فتكون أنت - بما أشارت إليه صفة الأكرمية على ما أنت فيه من الأمية - أعلم من أهل الأقلام

DURR-FULL:v8p560/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r1.claim: The author classifies the chapter as Meccan and counts nineteen verses.

DURR-FULL:v8p560/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r4.speaker: ابن شهاب
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r4.claim: Scholars he cites say the opening through ‘what he did not know’ was revealed at Hira and the rest came later.
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r4.anchor: عن ابن شهاب: حدثني محمد بن عباد بن جعفر المخزومي أنه سمع بعض علمائهم يقول

DURR-FULL:v8p560/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r6.claim: Aisha's account describes true dreams and retreat at Hira before Gabriel commands him to read, presses him three times, and recites the first five verses; Muhammad returns trembling to Khadija.
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r6.anchor: عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أنها قالت: أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصالحة في النوم

DURR-FULL:v8p561/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r7.claim: He identifies the first thing revealed as five verses, from ‘Read in the name of your Lord’ through ‘what he did not know.’
DURR-FULL:v8p561/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أول شيء أنزل من القرآن خمس آيات {اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق} إلى قوله: {ما لم يعلم}

DURR-FULL:v8p562/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r2.speaker: الزهري وعمرو بن دينار
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r2.claim: They report that at Hira an angel brought a brocade cloth inscribed with the first revelation through ‘what he did not know.’
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r2.anchor: عن الزهري وعمرو بن دينار أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء إذا أتاه ملك بنمط من ديباج

DURR-FULL:v8p562/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r3.speaker: عمرو بن جابر
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r3.claim: He transmits the same report of an angel at Hira bringing the opening passage written on brocade.
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r3.anchor: من طريق عمرو بن جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء إذا أتاه ملك بنمط من ديباج

DURR-FULL:v8p562/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r4.claim: His account says Gabriel pressed Muhammad, recited the opening through ‘what he did not know,’ and later revelation paused; the descent of al-Duha answered Khadija's worry that God had abandoned him.
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شداد قال: أتى جبريل محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا محمد اقرأ

DURR-FULL:v8p562/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r5.claim: Aisha relates the Prophet's retreat with Khadija, encounter with Gabriel and Michael, opening of his belly and chest, then command to read; he retained the verses thereafter.
DURR-FULL:v8p562/r5.anchor: عن عائشة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اعتكف هو وخديجة شهرا فوافق ذلك رمضان

DURR-FULL:v8p563/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r4.claim: He glosses teaching humanity what it did not know as teaching writing.
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r4.anchor: وفي قوله: {علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم} قال: الخط

DURR-FULL:v8p563/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r5.claim: He says the seeker of knowledge and seeker of worldly wealth are both insatiable but unequal: knowledge increases God's approval, while wealth-seeking deepens transgression; he cites two verses.
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: منهومان لا يشبعان: صاحب علم وصاحب دنيا ولا يستويان

TAB:96:5/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:5/r1.speaker: author
TAB:96:5/r1.claim: God taught humanity writing with the pen, along with other things it had not known.
TAB:96:5/r1.anchor: علم الإنسان الخط بالقلم ،   ولم يكن يعلمه

TAB:96:5/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:5/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:96:5/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd specifically says God taught people to write with the pen.
TAB:96:5/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  ( علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم ) قال :  علم الإنسان خطا بالقلم

BURHAN:v4p400/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p400/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p400/r4.claim: Ma is declarative or relative before laysa, lam, or la, and after illa, as in the cited examples.
BURHAN:v4p400/r4.anchor: إذا جاءت قبل ليس أو لم أو لا أو بعد إلا فإنها تكون خبرية

BURHAN:v1p377/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p377/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BURHAN:v1p377/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Ishmael was the first to establish Arabic writing, though reports on this subject are numerous and conflicting.
BURHAN:v1p377/r1.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يقول أول من وضع الكتاب العربى إسماعيل عليه السلام قال والروايات فى هذا الباب كثيرة ومختلفة

BURHAN:v1p377/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p377/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p377/r2.claim: The author holds that writing was divinely taught, citing God’s teaching by the pen and the Quranic oath by the pen; Adam and other prophets may have been taught it.
BURHAN:v1p377/r2.anchor: والذى نقوله إن الخط توقيفي لقوله ﴿ علم بالقلم علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم ﴾ وقال تعالى ﴿ ن والقلم وما يسطرون ﴾

BURHAN:v1p377/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p377/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p377/r3.claim: Some claim ancient Arabs did not know letter names, grammar, case, or hamza; the author answers that letter names were among what God taught Adam.
BURHAN:v1p377/r3.anchor: وزعم قوم أن العرب العاربة لم تعرف هذه الحروف بأسمائها وانهم لم يعرفوا نحوا ولا إعرابا

BURHAN:v1p377/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p377/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p377/r4.claim: The author accepts that Abu al-Aswad established Arabic grammar and al-Khalil prosody, but says the sciences existed earlier, declined, and were revived by the two imams.
BURHAN:v1p377/r4.anchor: وما اشتهر أن أبا الأسود أول من وضع العربية وأن الخليل أول من وضع العروض فلا ننكره

BURHAN:v1p377/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p377/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p377/r5.claim: Ancient codex spelling distinguishes words with wāw and yāʾ and omits hamza after a quiescent letter; this shows early Muslims knew orthography, and some scholars opposed abandoning codex spelling.
BURHAN:v1p377/r5.anchor: ومن الدليل على عرفان القدماء من الصحابة وغيرهم ذلك كتابتهم المصحف على الذى يعلله النحويون

BURHAN:v1p377/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p377/r6.speaker: الفراء
BURHAN:v1p377/r6.claim: Al-Farra says following the codex is preferable when its spelling has a valid basis in Arabic usage.
BURHAN:v1p377/r6.anchor: وأسند إلى الفراء قال اتباع المصحف إذا وجدت له وجها من كلام العرب

BURHAN:v1p377/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p377/r7.speaker: مالك
BURHAN:v1p377/r7.claim: Malik says codices must retain the first orthography; al-Dani reports no scholar opposed him. Malik also forbids changing extra written wāw and alif absent from pronunciation, as in أولوا, أولات, and الربوا.
BURHAN:v1p377/r7.anchor: وقال أشهب سئل مالك رحمه الله هل تكتب المصحف على ما أخذته الناس من الهجاء فقال لا إلا على الكتبة الأولى

BURHAN:v4p315/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p315/r3.speaker: أبو حاتم
BURHAN:v4p315/r3.claim: Abu Hatim says kalla is an opening particle meaning ألا; he adduces Gabriel's first five verses of al-Alaq, the pause after 96:5, and the later revelation beginning with kalla at 96:6.
BURHAN:v4p315/r3.anchor: فدل على إن الابتداء ب كلا من طريق الوحي فهي في الابتداء بمعنى ألا عنده

ITQAN:v3p284/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p284/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p284/r3.claim: The opening of “Read” similarly previews the Qur’an: it commands reading, begins in God’s name, signals legal knowledge and the principles of religion, and reports God’s teaching of what humans did not know; it can therefore be called the Qur’an’s title.
ITQAN:v3p284/r3.anchor: وكذلك أول سورة ( اقرأ فإنها مشتملة على نظير ما اشتملت عليه الفاتحة من براعة الاستهلال

ITQAN:v3p196/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p196/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p196/r1.claim: Repeating al-insan creates paronomasia: the first is humanity as a species, the second may be Adam, a literate person, or Idris, and the third is Abu Jahl.
ITQAN:v3p196/r1.anchor: ومثله ابن الصائغ بقوله ﴿ خلق الإنسان من علق ﴾ ثم قال ﴿ علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم كلا إن الإنسان ليطغى

ITQAN:v1p74/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p74/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p74/r1.claim: Of the reports about the first revelation, the soundest view is that it began with اقرأ باسم ربك; Aisha’s report in the two Sahih collections recounts the true dreams, retreat at Hira, and Gabriel’s three commands to read through ما لم يعلم.
ITQAN:v1p74/r1.anchor: أحدها وهو الصحيح ﴿ اقرأ باسم ربك ﴾

ITQAN:v4p442/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p442/r5.speaker: ابن فارس
ITQAN:v4p442/r5.claim: Ibn Faris argues that script was taught by God, citing the verses about the Pen and teaching humanity; these letters belong among the names taught to Adam.
ITQAN:v4p442/r5.anchor: وقال ابن فارس الذي نقوله إن الخط توقيفي لقوله تعالى

ITQAN:v1p109/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p109/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p109/r1.claim: Most of the Qur’an descended gradually; among short suras, the first revelation from al-Alaq ended at what he did not know, while al-Duha’s first portion ended at its being pleased, according to al-Tabarani’s hadith.
ITQAN:v1p109/r1.anchor: الأول غالب القرآن ومن أمثلته في السور القصار ﴿ اقرأ ﴾ أول ما نزل منها إلى قوله ﴿ ما لم يعلم ﴾ والضحى أول ما نزل منها

ITQAN:v1p109/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p109/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p109/r2.claim: The Fatiha, Ikhlas, Kawthar, Tabbat, Bayyina, Nasr, and the two Muawwidhatayn are examples of suras revealed together.
ITQAN:v1p109/r2.anchor: ومن أمثلة الثاني سورة الفاتحة والإخلاص والكوثر وتبت ولم يكن والنصر والمعوذتان نزلتا معا

ITQAN:v1p109/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p109/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v1p109/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reports that al-Mursalat was revealed to the Prophet in a cave while he recited it directly from the Prophet’s still-moist mouth.
ITQAN:v1p109/r3.anchor: ففي المستدرك عن ابن مسعود قال كنا مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في غار فنزلت عليه ﴿ والمرسلات عرفا ﴾

ITQAN:v1p109/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p109/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v1p109/r4.claim: Ibn Masud was unsure which of two verses was the ending he heard the Prophet recite: “What discourse after it will they believe?” or “When told to bow, they do not bow.”
ITQAN:v1p109/r4.anchor: فلا أدري بأيها ختم ﴿ فبأي حديث بعده يؤمنون ﴾ أو ﴿ وإذا قيل لهم اركعوا لا يركعون ﴾

ITQAN:v1p109/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p109/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p109/r5.claim: Al-Saff is another example of a sura revealed together, according to a hadith cited earlier in the work.
ITQAN:v1p109/r5.anchor: ومنه سورة الصف لحديثها السابق في النوع الأول

ITQAN:v1p109/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p109/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p109/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-Anam was revealed in Mecca at night as a whole, accompanied by seventy thousand angels.
ITQAN:v1p109/r6.anchor: فقد أخرج أبو عبيد والطبراني عن ابن عباس قال نزلت سورة الأنعام بمكة ليلا جملة حولها سبعون ألف ملك

ITQAN:v1p109/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p109/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
ITQAN:v1p109/r7.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet from Ibn Umar says al-Anam descended all at once with seventy thousand angels; its chain includes Yusuf ibn Atiyya, whom the source calls abandoned.
ITQAN:v1p109/r7.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني من طريق يوسف بن عطية الصفار وهو متروك عن ابن عون عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نزلت علي سورة الأنعام جملة واحدة

ITQAN:v1p109/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p109/r8.speaker: علي
ITQAN:v1p109/r8.claim: Ali says the Qur’an came in groups of five except al-Anam, which descended whole with a thousand angels, seventy from each heaven; the chain contains an unknown narrator.
ITQAN:v1p109/r8.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي في الشعب بسند فيه من لا يعرف عن علي قال أنزل القرآن خمسا خمسا إلا سورة الأنعام

ITQAN:v1p109/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p109/r9.speaker: أبي بن كعب
ITQAN:v1p109/r9.claim: A report raised to the Prophet from Ubayy ibn Kab says al-Anam descended whole, accompanied by seventy thousand angels.
ITQAN:v1p109/r9.anchor: وأخرج أبو الشيخ عن أبي بن كعب مرفوعا أنزلت علي سورة الأنعام جملة واحدة يشيعها سبعون ألف ملك

ITQAN:v1p109/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p109/r10.speaker: مجاهد
ITQAN:v1p109/r10.claim: Mujahid says all of al-Anam descended at once with five hundred angels.
ITQAN:v1p109/r10.anchor: وأخرج عن مجاهد قال نزلت الأنعام كلها جملة واحدة معها خمسمائة ملك

ITQAN:v1p109/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p109/r11.speaker: عطاء
ITQAN:v1p109/r11.claim: Ata says al-Anam descended in its entirety with seventy thousand angels.
ITQAN:v1p109/r11.anchor: وأخرج عن عطاء قال أنزلت الأنعام جميعا ومعها سبعون ألف ملك

ITQAN:v1p109/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p109/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p109/r12.claim: Al-Suyuti says these supporting reports strengthen one another.

ITQAN:v1p109/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p109/r13.speaker: ابن الصلاح
ITQAN:v1p109/r13.claim: Ibn al-Salah says the report that al-Anam descended all at once has a weak chain from Ubayy, and he found no sound chain for it.
ITQAN:v1p109/r13.anchor: وقال ابن الصلاح في فتاويه الحديث الوارد في أنها نزلت جملة رويناه من طريق أبي بن كعب وفي إسناده ضعف

ITQAN:v1p109/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p109/r14.speaker: ابن الصلاح
ITQAN:v1p109/r14.claim: Ibn al-Salah notes contrary reports that al-Anam was not wholly revealed at once but had verses revealed in Medina; the proposed number varies between three, six, or another count.
ITQAN:v1p109/r14.anchor: وقد روي ما يخالفه فروي أنها لم تنزل جملة واحدة بل نزلت آيات منها بالمدينة اختلفوا في عددها فقيل ثلاث وقيل ست

ITQAN:v4p478/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p478/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p478/r1.claim: Anyone can recognize facial beauty, but speech requires cultivated literary taste; grammar, language, or law alone does not qualify someone to judge discourse, so critics should be trained in rhetoric, prose, sermons, writing, and poetry.
ITQAN:v4p478/r1.anchor: وأما الكلام فلا يدرك إلا بالذوق وليس كل من إشتغل بالنحو واللغة والفقه يكون من أهل الذوق

ITQAN:v4p478/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p478/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v4p478/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says a Qur’an interpreter must preserve its elegant structure and complete rhetoric, leaving intact the quality that made it a challenge.
ITQAN:v4p478/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري من حق مفسر كتاب الله الباهر وكلامه المعجز أن يتعاهد بقاء النظم على حسنه والبلاغة على كمالها

ITQAN:v4p478/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p478/r3.speaker: غيره
ITQAN:v4p478/r3.claim: Another authority calls mastery of rhetoric central to tafsir and the foundation of eloquence that reveals the wonders of God’s speech.
ITQAN:v4p478/r3.anchor: وقال غيره معرفة هذه الصناعة بأوضاعها هي عمدة التفسير المطلع على عجائب كلام الله تعالى

ITQAN:v4p478/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p478/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p478/r4.claim: Knowledge of Qur’anic readings shows how to pronounce the text and helps prefer one of several possible interpretations.
ITQAN:v4p478/r4.anchor: الثامن علم القراءات لأن به يعرف كيفية النطق بالقرآن وبالقراءات يترجح بعض الوجوه المحتملة على بعض

ITQAN:v4p478/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p478/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p478/r5.claim: Principles of religion help interpret verses whose apparent wording attributes what is impossible to God and establish what is necessary, impossible, or possible.
ITQAN:v4p478/r5.anchor: التاسع أصول الدين بما في القرآن من الآيات الدالة بظاهرها على ما لا يجوز على الله تعالى

ITQAN:v4p478/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p478/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p478/r6.claim: Legal theory is needed to understand how rulings are inferred and derived.
ITQAN:v4p478/r6.anchor: العاشر أصول الفقه إذ به يعرف وجه الاستدلال على الأحكام والإستنباط

ITQAN:v4p478/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p478/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p478/r7.claim: Knowledge of occasions of revelation and narratives explains a verse’s meaning in light of the circumstances in which it was revealed.
ITQAN:v4p478/r7.anchor: الحادي عشر أسباب النزول والقصص إذ بسبب النزول يعرف معنى الآية المنزلة فيه بحسب ما أنزلت فيه

ITQAN:v4p478/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p478/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p478/r8.claim: Knowledge of abrogating and abrogated material distinguishes decisive verses from others.
ITQAN:v4p478/r8.anchor: الثاني عشر الناسخ والمنسوخ ليعلم المحكم من غيره

ITQAN:v4p478/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p478/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p478/r9.claim: Fiqh is one of the disciplines required for tafsir.
ITQAN:v4p478/r9.anchor:
6329 الثالث عشر الفقه
6330 الرابع عشر الأحاديث المبينة لتفسير المجمل والمبهم

ITQAN:v4p478/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p478/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p478/r10.claim: Hadith is needed to explain what is general or ambiguous in the Qur’an.
ITQAN:v4p478/r10.anchor: الرابع عشر الأحاديث المبينة لتفسير المجمل والمبهم

ITQAN:v4p478/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p478/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p478/r11.claim: Inspired knowledge is granted by God to those who act on what they know; a hadith says God will teach such a person what they did not know.
ITQAN:v4p478/r11.anchor: الخامس عشر علم الموهبة وهو علم يورثه الله تعالى لمن عمل بما علم وإليه الإشارة بحديث ( من عمل بما علم ورثه الله علم ما لم يعلم )

ITQAN:v4p478/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p478/r12.speaker: ابن أبي الدنيا
ITQAN:v4p478/r12.claim: Ibn Abi al-Dunya says the Qur’anic sciences and what can be derived from them form an endless ocean.
ITQAN:v4p478/r12.anchor: قال ابن أبي الدنيا وعلوم القرآن وما يستنبط منه بحر لا ساحل له

ITQAN:v4p478/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p478/r13.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p478/r13.claim: These disciplines are prerequisites for an exegete: interpreting without them is the forbidden interpretation by opinion, while interpreting with them is not.
ITQAN:v4p478/r13.anchor: قال فهذه العلوم التي هي كالآية للمفسر لا يكون مفسرا إلا بتحصيلها فمن فسر بدونها كان مفسرا بالرأي المنهي عنه

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r1.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha says revelation began with true dreams and seclusion at Ḥirāʾ; Gabriel's repeated commands to recite introduced al-ʿAlaq, and the shaken Prophet was comforted by Khadīja, who cited his virtues. Al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmit it.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r1.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها قالت: "أول ما بدئ به رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة في النوم

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r2.speaker: بعض علمائهم
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r2.claim: Ibn Shihāb relays from Muḥammad b. ʿAbbād that some scholars said al-ʿAlaq's first five verses were revealed at Ḥirāʾ; the remainder came later as God willed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r2.anchor: أنه سمع بعض علمائهم يقول: كان أول ما أنزل الله على رسوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - {اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق

NASHR:v1p40/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p40/r1.speaker: أئمة أهل العراق
NASHR:v1p40/r1.claim: Iraqi imams who accepted the ten and eleven readings as firmly established as the seven compiled them and recited them in and out of prayer; the author says scholars agreed and none objected.
NASHR:v1p40/r1.anchor: كان أئمة أهل العراق الذين ثبتت عندهم قراءات العشرة والأحد عشر كثبوت هذه السبعة

NASHR:v1p40/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p40/r2.speaker: القاضي عياض
NASHR:v1p40/r2.claim: The condemnation reported by Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ against Ibn Shanabūdh concerned anomalous readings outside the Uthmanic codex, not the canonical ten.
NASHR:v1p40/r2.anchor: وأما الذي ذكره القاضي عياض ومن نقل كلامه من الإنكار على ابن شنبوذ

NASHR:v1p40/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p40/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p40/r3.claim: A reader may recite a transmitted reading he knows but must not use one he has not learned; he should neither reject nor oppose another reader for a reading known to that person.
NASHR:v1p40/r3.anchor: فليس له أن يقرأ بما لا يعلمه، فإن القراءة كما قال زيد بن ثابت سنة

NASHR:v1p40/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p40/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p40/r4.claim: The seven readings attributed to Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim are not the seven revealed aḥruf, nor do the seven readings together constitute one of those aḥruf; the author says scholars agree.
NASHR:v1p40/r4.anchor: فتبين بما ذكرناه أن القراءات المنسوبة إلى نافع وعاصم ليست هي الأحرف السبعة

NASHR:v1p40/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p40/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p40/r5.claim: Readings established from al-Aʿmash, Yaʿqūb, Khalaf, Abū Jaʿfar, and Shaybah stand like those of the seven for readers who establish their transmission; the author says the imams did not dispute this.
NASHR:v1p40/r5.anchor: بل القراءات الثابتة عن الأئمة القراء: كالأعمش ويعقوب وخلف وأبي جعفر، وشيبة

NASHR:v1p40/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p40/r6.speaker: المتأخرون
NASHR:v1p40/r6.claim: The later scholars' dispute was whether the Uthmanic codex, including the seven, ten, and other readings it contains, represents one of the seven revealed aḥruf.
NASHR:v1p40/r6.anchor: وإنما تنازع الناس من الخلف في المصحف العثماني الإمام الذي أجمع عليه أصحاب رسول الله

AZRAQI:v2p204/r1.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p204/r1.speaker: عائشة
AZRAQI:v2p204/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha says the Prophet's first revelation came as truthful dreams that appeared as clearly as daybreak.
AZRAQI:v2p204/r1.anchor: عن عايشة رضي الله عنها أنها قالت أول ما بدي به رسول الله & من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة في النوم

AZRAQI:v2p204/r2.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p204/r2.speaker: عائشة
AZRAQI:v2p204/r2.claim: Afterward the Prophet loved solitude and repeatedly spent several nights worshipping and seeking righteousness in Ḥirāʾ, taking provisions and returning to Khadīja for more.
AZRAQI:v2p204/r2.anchor: فكان لا يرى رؤيا لا جاءته مثل فقل الصبح ثم حبب إليه الخلاء فكان يأتي حراء

AZRAQI:v2p204/r3.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p204/r3.speaker: عائشة
AZRAQI:v2p204/r3.claim: In Ḥirāʾ Gabriel commands him to read three times and squeezes him hard; after asking what to read, the Prophet recites the opening of sūrat al-ʿAlaq through this verse.
AZRAQI:v2p204/r3.anchor: عن معمر أخبرني الزهري عن عروة عن عايشة رضي الله عنها أنها قالت أول ما بدي به رسول الله

AZRAQI:v2p204/r4.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p204/r4.speaker: ابن أبي مليكة
AZRAQI:v2p204/r4.claim: Ibn Abī Mulayka reports that Gabriel greeted Khadīja on God's behalf and promised her a quiet, fatigue-free house in Paradise; the Prophet conveys it, and she returns greetings to God and Gabriel.
AZRAQI:v2p204/r4.anchor: قال سمعت ابن أبي مليكة يقول جاءت خديجة إلى النبي & بحيس وهو بحراء فجاءه جبريل

IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r1.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r1.claim: Ibn Hisham says Arabs use both taḥannuth and taḥannuf intending ḥanīfiyya, substituting f for th as in jadath and jadaf; Ru'ba's line with al-ajdaf illustrates that sound change.
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r1.anchor: قال رؤبة ابن العجاج: لو كان أحجاري مع الأجداف

IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda reports that Arabs also say fam in place of thumma, substituting f for th.
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r2.anchor: وحدثني أبو عبيدة أن العرب تقول: فم، في موضع ثم، يبدلون الفاء من الثاء

IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r3.speaker: عبيد
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r3.claim: Ubayd's report says Muhammad annually secluded himself at Hira during Ramadan, fed the poor, and returned to circumambulate the Kaaba; Gabriel then came with a written silk cloth and commanded him to recite, repeating the embrace three times, after which Muhammad woke with the words fixed in his heart.
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r3.anchor: قال عبيد: فكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجاور ذلك الشهر من كل سنة، يطعم من جاءه من المساكين

ABUHAYYAN:96:5/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:5/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:5/r1.claim: The apparent meaning of الإنسان is the human species, whose acquisition of knowledge after ignorance is being recounted.
ABUHAYYAN:96:5/r1.anchor: والإنسان في قوله : { علم الإنسان } ، الظاهر أنه اسم الجنس ، عدد عليه اكتساب العلوم بعد الجهل بها

ABUHAYYAN:96:5/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:5/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:96:5/r2.claim: Another view takes الإنسان here to mean the Messenger.

ALUSI:96:5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:5/r1.claim: The statement that God taught humanity what it did not know is an appositional elaboration of teaching by the pen: He teaches with or without it, across all kinds of knowledge.
ALUSI:96:5/r1.anchor: أي علمه به وبدونه من الأمور الكلية والجزئية والجلية والخفية

ALUSI:96:5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:5/r2.speaker: الإرشاد
ALUSI:96:5/r2.claim: Al-Irshād says the omitted first object and the second object’s description as previously unknown display God’s power and generosity, and hint that He will teach the Prophet knowledge beyond human comprehension.
ALUSI:96:5/r2.anchor: من الدلالة على كمال قدرته تعالى

ALUSI:96:5/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:5/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:5/r10.claim: If recitation is for conveying, the Prophet is to proclaim to his people that his generous Lord rewards him and strengthens him to memorize and deliver the Qur’an.
ALUSI:96:5/r10.anchor: الذي يثيبك على عملك بما يقتضيه كرمه ويقويك على حفظ القرآن لتبلغه

ALUSI:96:6/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:6/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:6/r5.claim: Some supply an omitted thought after verse 5: the human should have thanked God for these great favors, but instead transgressed and disbelieved.
ALUSI:96:6/r5.anchor: ليشكر تلك النعم الجليلة فطغى وكفر كلا

BAGHAWI:96:1/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:1/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI:96:1/r2.claim: Most commentators hold that this was the first sūra revealed and that the first revelation was its opening five verses, ending with “what he did not know.”
BAGHAWI:96:1/r2.anchor: أكثر المفسرين : على أن هذه السورة أول سورة نزلت من القرآن ، وأول ما نزل خمس آيات

BAGHAWI:96:1/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:1/r3.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI:96:1/r3.claim: Aisha recounts the Prophet’s true dreams, retreat and worship at Hira, then Gabriel’s command to read and three forceful embraces before reciting the opening revelation; Baghawi gives no grading.
BAGHAWI:96:1/r3.anchor: عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أنها قالت : " أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصالحة

BAGHAWI:96:1/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:1/r4.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI:96:1/r4.claim: After the revelation the frightened Prophet returned to Khadija, who reassured him that God would never disgrace him because he maintained kinship, supported the needy, hosted guests, and aided people in hardship.
BAGHAWI:96:1/r4.anchor: فقالت خديجة : كلا ، والله ما يخزيك الله أبداً ، إنك لتصل الرحم ، وتحمل الكل ، وتكسب المعدوم

BAGHAWI:96:1/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:1/r6.speaker: الزهري
BAGHAWI:96:1/r6.claim: In a Bukhari version, al-Zuhri adds that revelation paused and the Prophet, in grief, repeatedly approached mountain peaks intending to throw himself down until Gabriel reassured him; the addition is introduced as “what reached us.”
BAGHAWI:96:1/r6.anchor: حتى حزن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما بلغنا حزناً غدا منه مراراً حتى يتردى من رؤوس شواهق الجبال

BAGHAWI:96:5/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:5/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:5/r1.claim: God taught humanity the various kinds of guidance and clear expression.
BAGHAWI:96:5/r1.anchor: علم الإنسان مالم يعلم } من أنواع الهدى والبيان

BAGHAWI:96:5/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:5/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI:96:5/r2.claim: An alternative view identifies the human taught as Adam, whom God taught all the names.

BAGHAWI:96:5/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:5/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI:96:5/r3.claim: Another view identifies the human as Muhammad, supported by the statement that God taught him what he did not know.
BAGHAWI:96:5/r3.anchor: وقيل : الإنسان ها هنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI:96:5/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:5/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:5/r1.claim: God teaches through created faculties, established signs, and revealed verses, enabling even the unlettered Prophet to read.
BAYDAWI:96:5/r1.anchor: فيعلمك القراءة وإن لم تكن قارئا

BAYDAWI:96:5/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:5/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:5/r2.claim: The passage recalls humanity's movement from the lowest to the highest state, proving God's lordship and generosity; it first signals rational knowledge, then revealed knowledge.
BAYDAWI:96:5/r2.anchor: وقد عدد سبحانه وتعالى مبدأ أمر الإنسان ومنتهاه إظهارا لما أنعم عليه من أن نقله من أخس المراتب إلى أعلاها

BIQAI:96:5/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:5/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:5/r1.claim: Writing's immeasurable benefits support the ordered affairs of religion and worldly life in both worlds, demonstrating God's subtle wisdom and providential management.
BIQAI:96:5/r1.anchor: ما في الكتابة من المنافع التي لا يحيط بها غيره سبحانه وتعالى

BIQAI:96:5/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:5/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:5/r2.claim: The human is inclined to remain familiar with his present condition rather than move beyond it, and forgets what his Lord does not inspire him to retain.
BIQAI:96:5/r2.anchor: الذي من شأنه الأنس بما هو فيه لا ينتقل إلى غيره

BIQAI:96:5/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:5/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:5/r3.claim: God gently teaches what people did not know: religious knowledge from Scripture and Sunna, worldly dealings and crafts, and immediate knowledge without an apparent cause.
BIQAI:96:5/r3.anchor: لينتظم به حاله في دينه من الكتاب والسنة ودنياه من المعاملات والصنائع

BIQAI:96:5/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:5/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:5/r4.claim: God's uncaused, bestowed knowledge lets a person order premises through definitions and middle terms to infer conclusions and recognize intuitive truths; it complements created faculties, signs, and revealed verses.
BIQAI:96:5/r4.anchor: ما يعرف به ترتيب المقدمات بالحدود والوسطى

BIQAI:96:5/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:5/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:5/r5.claim: If knowledge came only through ordinary causes, people would be equal in time spent learning and initial knowledge, just as they are in gestation and human origin.
BIQAI:96:5/r5.anchor: ولو كان ذلك بالأسباب فقط لتساوى الناس في مدة التعليم

BIQAI:96:5/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:5/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:5/r6.claim: God's mention of the human's beginning and end, moving him from the lowest state to the highest, establishes divine lordship and confirms His supreme generosity.
BIQAI:96:5/r6.anchor: وقد ذكر سبحانه مبدأ الإنسان ومنتهاه بنقله من أخس الحالات إلى أعلاها

BIQAI:96:5/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:5/r7.speaker: الملوي
BIQAI:96:5/r7.claim: Al-Malawī argues that knowledge is the noblest gift: had any gift or blessing been more excellent, God would have mentioned it after describing Himself as most generous.
BIQAI:96:5/r7.anchor: قال الملوي : ولو كان شيء من العطاء والنعم أشرف من العلم

BIQAI:96:5/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:5/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:5/r8.claim: The verse also signals the heightened generosity of scholars who teach others.
BIQAI:96:5/r8.anchor: وفي ذلك إشارة إلى مزيد كرم العلماء بالتعليم

BIQAI:96:5/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:5/r9.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI:96:5/r9.claim: Al-Rāzī says that each of the worlds of creation and command has both a specific and a general aspect.
BIQAI:96:5/r9.anchor: قال الرازي : وفي كل من العالمين خصوص وعموم

BIQAI:96:5/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:5/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:5/r10.claim: Though unlettered and presently knowing nothing, the Prophet will be taught by God's generosity and become more learned than people of the pen and higher than every lofty rank.
BIQAI:96:5/r10.anchor: يعلمك أيها النبي الكريم وإن كنت أمياً لا تعلم الآن شيئاً

DURR:96:1/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r3.speaker: بعض علمائهم
DURR:96:1/r3.claim: Scholars heard by Muḥammad b. ʿAbbād said the opening through 96:5 was revealed at Ḥirāʾ; the sūra’s ending came later as God willed.
DURR:96:1/r3.anchor: عن ابن شهاب : حدثني محمد بن عباد بن جعفر المخزومي أنه سمع بعض علمائهم يقول

DURR:96:1/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r6.speaker: عائشة
DURR:96:1/r6.claim: In ʿĀʾisha’s account, Gabriel commanded the unlettered Prophet to recite, squeezed him three times, then delivered the opening five verses at Ḥirāʾ.
DURR:96:1/r6.anchor: عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أنها قالت : «أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصالحة

DURR:96:1/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:96:1/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the first revelation consisted of five verses, ending with “what he did not know.”
DURR:96:1/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : أول شيء أنزل من القرآن خمس آيات { اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق } إلى قوله : { ما لم يعلم } .

DURR:96:1/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r15.speaker: الزهري وعمرو بن دينار
DURR:96:1/r15.claim: Al-Zuhrī and ʿAmr b. Dīnār report that, at Ḥirāʾ, an angel brought the Prophet brocade bearing the opening five verses in writing.
DURR:96:1/r15.anchor: عن الزهري وعمرو بن دينار أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء إذا أتاه ملك بنمط من ديباج

DURR:96:1/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r16.speaker: عمرو بن جابر
DURR:96:1/r16.claim: ʿAmr b. Jābir likewise reports that an angel came to the Prophet at Ḥirāʾ with brocade inscribed through “what he did not know.”
DURR:96:1/r16.anchor: من طريق عمرو بن جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء إذ أتاه ملك

DURR:96:1/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r17.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
DURR:96:1/r17.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. Shaddād recounts Gabriel’s repeated command to recite and squeezing of Muhammad, who then received the opening passage through 96:5.
DURR:96:1/r17.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شداد قال : «أتى جبريل محمداً صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : يا محمد اقرأ

DURR:96:1/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r19.speaker: عائشة
DURR:96:1/r19.claim: A second ʿĀʾisha account describes Gabriel’s vast appearance, washing the Prophet’s opened chest, teaching the opening five verses, and weighing him against men; Michael says his community will follow.
DURR:96:1/r19.anchor: عن عائشة «أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اعتكف هو وخديجة شهراً فوافق ذلك رمضان

DURR:96:4/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:4/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR:96:4/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses God’s teaching humanity what it did not know as teaching writing.
DURR:96:4/r2.anchor: وفي قوله : { علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم } قال : الخط .

DURR:96:5/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:5/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR:96:5/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses God’s teaching humanity what it did not know as teaching writing.
DURR:96:5/r2.anchor: وفي قوله : { علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم } قال : الخط .

BUKHARI:4953/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4953/r1.speaker: عائشة
BUKHARI:4953/r1.claim: Aisha reports true dreams and worship in Hira before Gabriel pressed Muhammad three times, met his 'I cannot read,' then recited the opening revelation through 96:5; Muhammad returned trembling, and revelation later paused after Waraqa died.
BUKHARI:4953/r1.anchor: أن عائشة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت كان أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الرؤيا الصادقة في النوم

BUKHARI:4953/r2.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4953/r2.speaker: author
BUKHARI:4953/r2.claim: The report glosses the Prophet's tahannuth in Hira as worship.
BUKHARI:4953/r2.anchor: فيتحنث فيه قال والتحنث التعبد الليالي

BUKHARI:4953/r3.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4953/r3.speaker: خديجة
BUKHARI:4953/r3.claim: Khadija reassures Muhammad that God will not disgrace him, citing his care for kin, honesty, service to the needy, hospitality, and help in righteous crises.
BUKHARI:4953/r3.anchor: قَالَتْ خَدِيجَةُ كَلاَّ أَبْشِرْ، فَوَاللَّهِ لاَ يُخْزِيكَ اللَّهُ أَبَدًا، فَوَاللَّهِ إِنَّكَ لَتَصِلُ الرَّحِمَ

BUKHARI:4953/r4.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4953/r4.speaker: author
BUKHARI:4953/r4.claim: The narrative identifies Waraqa as Khadija's cousin, a pre-Islamic Christian who wrote Arabic and Gospel passages in Arabic; he was elderly and blind.
BUKHARI:4953/r4.anchor: وَرَقَةَ بْنِ نَوْفَلٍ وَهْوَ ابْنُ عَمِّ خَدِيجَةَ أَخِي أَبِيهَا، وَكَانَ امْرَأً تَنَصَّرَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ

BUKHARI:4953/r5.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4953/r5.speaker: ورقة
BUKHARI:4953/r5.claim: Waraqa identifies the visitor as the namus sent to Moses and wishes he were young and alive to help Muhammad.
BUKHARI:4953/r5.anchor: فَقَالَ وَرَقَةُ هَذَا النَّامُوسُ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ عَلَى مُوسَى، لَيْتَنِي فِيهَا جَذَعًا، لَيْتَنِي أَكُونُ حَيًّا

BUKHARI:4953/r6.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4953/r6.speaker: ورقة
BUKHARI:4953/r6.claim: Waraqa says that anyone bringing such a message is harmed and promises Muhammad strong support if he lives to see that day.
BUKHARI:4953/r6.anchor: قَالَ وَرَقَةُ نَعَمْ لَمْ يَأْتِ رَجُلٌ بِمَا جِئْتَ بِهِ إِلاَّ أُوذِيَ، وَإِنْ يُدْرِكْنِي يَوْمُكَ حَيًّا أَنْصُرَكَ نَصْرًا مُؤَزَّرًا

BUKHARI:6982/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:6982/r1.speaker: عائشة
BUKHARI:6982/r1.claim: Aisha reports true dreams preceding worship in Hira, then Gabriel's three embraces and recitation of the opening verses through 96:5; Muhammad returned trembling, asked to be covered, and feared for himself.
BUKHARI:6982/r1.anchor: عَنْ عَائِشَةَ ـ رضى الله عنها ـ أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ أَوَّلُ مَا بُدِئَ بِهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنَ الْوَحْىِ الرُّؤْيَا الصَّادِقَةُ

BUKHARI:6982/r2.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:6982/r2.speaker: author
BUKHARI:6982/r2.claim: The report glosses the Prophet's tahannuth in Hira as worship.
BUKHARI:6982/r2.anchor: فيتحنث فيه وهو التعبد الليالي ذوات العدد

BUKHARI:6982/r3.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:6982/r3.speaker: خديجة
BUKHARI:6982/r3.claim: Khadija comforts Muhammad, assuring him God will not disgrace him because he maintains kinship, tells the truth, bears burdens, feeds guests, and helps in right causes.

BUKHARI:6982/r4.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:6982/r4.speaker: author
BUKHARI:6982/r4.claim: The narrative identifies Waraqa as Khadija's cousin, a pre-Islamic Christian who wrote Arabic and Gospel passages in Arabic; he was elderly and blind.
BUKHARI:6982/r4.anchor: وَرَقَةَ بْنِ نَوْفَلِ بْنِ أَسَدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْعُزَّى بْنِ قُصَىٍّ ـ وَهُوَ ابْنُ عَمِّ خَدِيجَةَ أَخُو أَبِيهَا، وَكَانَ امْرَأً تَنَصَّرَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ

BUKHARI:6982/r5.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:6982/r5.speaker: ورقة
BUKHARI:6982/r5.claim: Waraqa identifies the visitor as the messenger sent to Moses and wishes he could live until Muhammad's people expel him.
BUKHARI:6982/r5.anchor: فَقَالَ وَرَقَةُ هَذَا النَّامُوسُ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ عَلَى مُوسَى، يَا لَيْتَنِي فِيهَا جَذَعًا أَكُونُ حَيًّا، حِينَ يُخْرِجُكَ قَوْمُكَ

BUKHARI:6982/r6.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:6982/r6.speaker: ورقة
BUKHARI:6982/r6.claim: Waraqa says anyone bringing this message will face opposition and pledges to support Muhammad if he lives to see the day.
BUKHARI:6982/r6.anchor: فَقَالَ وَرَقَةُ نَعَمْ، لَمْ يَأْتِ رَجُلٌ قَطُّ بِمَا جِئْتَ بِهِ إِلاَّ عُودِيَ، وَإِنْ يُدْرِكْنِي يَوْمُكَ أَنْصُرَكَ نَصْرًا مُؤَزَّرًا

BUKHARI:6982/r7.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:6982/r7.speaker: author
BUKHARI:6982/r7.claim: In an account introduced as what reached them, Muhammad repeatedly considered throwing himself from mountain summits during the pause; Gabriel affirmed his prophethood and calmed him.
BUKHARI:6982/r7.anchor: فِيمَا بَلَغَنَا حُزْنًا غَدَا مِنْهُ مِرَارًا كَىْ يَتَرَدَّى مِنْ رُءُوسِ شَوَاهِقِ الْجِبَالِ

IBNASHUR:96:1/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:1/r7.speaker: عائشة، أبو موسى الأشعري
IBNASHUR:96:1/r7.claim: Sound reports from Aisha establish that these first five verses were first, delivered to Muhammad in Hira on Ramadan 17, year 40 after the Elephant; Abu Musa and most exegetes agree.
IBNASHUR:96:1/r7.anchor: وهي أول سورة نزلت في القرآن كما ثبت في الأحاديث الصحيحة الواضحة ، ونزل أولها بغار حراء على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR:96:1/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:1/r17.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR:96:1/r17.claim: Aisha's report is Ibn Ashur's basis for identifying these five verses as the first revelation to Muhammad in Hira.
IBNASHUR:96:1/r17.anchor: هذا أول ما أوحي به من القرآن إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لما ثبت عن عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR:96:5/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:5/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:5/r1.claim: The clause “He taught the human what he did not know” is the predicate of “your Lord is most generous”; the intervening material is parenthetical.
IBNASHUR:96:5/r1.anchor: وجملة : { علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم } خبر عن قوله : { وربك الأكرم } وما بينهما اعتراض

IBNASHUR:96:5/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:5/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:5/r2.claim: The definite noun may be generic, broadening the account from teaching by the pen to God's teaching of humanity generally.
IBNASHUR:96:5/r2.anchor: وتعريف { الإنسان } يجوز أن يكون تعريف الجنس فيكون ارتقاء في الإِعلام

IBNASHUR:96:5/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:5/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:5/r3.claim: The two teachings point to three routes of knowledge: written records and reading books, oral instruction and dictation, and discoveries or inventions produced by reasoning; writing lets learning pass across distance and generations.
IBNASHUR:96:5/r3.anchor: وقد حصلتْ من ذكر التعليم بالقلم والتعليم الأعم إشارة إلى ما يتلقاه الإنسان من التعاليم سواء كان بالدرس أم بمطالعة الكتب

IBNASHUR:96:5/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:5/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:5/r4.claim: This reassures Muhammad that not knowing writing does not prevent him from reciting: God can teach him directly, without prior writing knowledge, as He taught literate people to read.
IBNASHUR:96:5/r4.anchor: وفي ذلك اطمئنان لنفس النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن عدم معرفته الكتابة لا يحول دون قراءته

IBNASHUR:96:5/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:5/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:5/r5.claim: The wording reminds Muhammad that knowledge is preceded by ignorance; inability to read writing is no reason to despair of learning the Qur'an and sharia.
IBNASHUR:96:5/r5.anchor: وأشعر قوله : { ما لم يعلم } أن العلم مسبوق بالجهل فكل علم يحصل فهو علم ما لم يكن يُعلَم من قبل

IBNASHUR:96:5/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:5/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:5/r6.claim: The verses signal God's concern that the revealed Qur'an be written down; Muhammad therefore appointed scribes for revelation from the beginning of his mission.
IBNASHUR:96:5/r6.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى الاهتمام بعلم الكتابة وبأن الله يريد أن يُكتَب للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم ما ينزل عليه من القرآن

IBNASHUR:96:5/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:5/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:5/r8.claim: These are the final verses of the five that were first revealed to Muhammad in the cave of Hira.
IBNASHUR:96:5/r8.anchor: وهذه آخر الخمس الآيات التي هي أول ما أنزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في غار حراء

IBNHIBBAN:v1p217/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:v1p217/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:v1p217/r1.claim: The Prophet recounts the first revelation: Gabriel pressed him three times, then recited 96:1–5; Khadīja comforted him and Waraqa identified the revelation as that given to Moses and predicted hostility, and Gabriel later reassured him after revelation paused.
IBNHIBBAN:v1p217/r1.anchor: ثم أرسلني فقال: {اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق} حتى بلغ {ما لم يعلم}

IBNATIYYA:96:5/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:5/r1.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA:96:5/r1.claim: One view says the human taught what he did not know refers specifically to Muḥammad.

IBNATIYYA:96:5/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:5/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:5/r2.claim: The clearer view is that al-insān means humankind as a class.
IBNATIYYA:96:5/r2.anchor: اسم الجنس وهو الأظهر ،   وعدد نعمته

IBNATIYYA:96:5/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:5/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:5/r3.claim: The verse counts among God's blessings the acquisition of knowledge after ignorance.
IBNATIYYA:96:5/r3.anchor: وعدد نعمته اكتساب المعارف بعد جهله بها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r1.speaker: عائشة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet interpreted only as many Quranic verses as Gabriel had taught him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r1.anchor: روي عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها قالت: «ما كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يفسر من كتاب الله إلا آيا بعدد علمه إياهن جبريل»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r2.claim: The author limits ʿĀʾisha’s report to unseen matters, ambiguous passages, and similar subjects whose explanation can only be known through divine instruction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r2.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق رضي الله عنه: ومعنى هذا الحديث: في مغيبات القرآن، وتفسير مجمله، ونحو هذا مما لا سبيل إليه إلا بتوقيف من الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r3.claim: Some unseen matters are inaccessible even by inference, such as the time of the Hour; others can be inferred from the wording, such as the number of trumpet blasts and the sequence of the heavens’ and earth’s creation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r3.anchor: ومن جملة مغيباته ما لم يعلم الله به كوقت قيام الساعة ونحوه، ومنها ما يستقرأ من ألفاظه كعدد النفخات في الصور، وكرتبة خلق السماوات والأرض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r4.claim: A Prophetic report warns that a person who speaks about the Quran from personal opinion errs even when what he says is correct.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r4.anchor: ويروى أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «من تكلم في القرآن برأيه فأصاب فقد أخطأ»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r5.claim: The author explains the warning as applying to someone who ventures an interpretation without considering scholarly precedent or the rules of disciplines such as grammar and legal theory.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r5.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق رضي الله عنه: ومعنى هذا أن يسأل الرجل عن معنى في كتاب الله فيتسور عليه برأيه، دون نظر فيما قال العلماء، أو اقتضته قوانين العلوم كالنحو، والأصول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r6.claim: The warning does not bar linguists, grammarians, and jurists from reasoned interpretation grounded in the rules of their disciplines; this is not mere personal opinion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r6.anchor: وليس يدخل في هذا الحديث أن يفسر اللغويون لغته، والنحاة نحوه، والفقهاء معانيه، ويقول كل واحد باجتهاده المبني على قوانين علم ونظر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r7.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r7.claim: Leading early authorities such as Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib and ʿĀmir al-Shaʿbī refrained from interpreting the Quran out of caution, despite their learning and standing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r7.anchor: وكان جلة من السلف كسعيد بن المسيب، وعامر الشعبي، وغيرهما، يعظمون تفسير القرآن، ويتوقفون عنه تورعا واحتياطا لأنفسهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r8.claim: The author also notes that many other eminent early Muslims interpreted the Quran and thereby preserved its exegesis for the Muslim community.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r8.anchor: وكان جلة من السلف كثير عددهم يفسرونه وهم أبقوا على المسلمين في ذلك رضي الله عنهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r9.claim: The author ranks ʿAlī as the foremost interpreter, followed by Ibn ʿAbbās, who devoted himself fully to the field; later scholars including Mujāhid and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr followed Ibn ʿAbbās, whose transmitted exegesis is more extensive than ʿAlī’s.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r9.anchor: فأما صدر المفسرين والمؤيد فيهم فعلي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه، ويتلوه عبد الله بن العباس رضي الله عنهما، وهو تجرد للأمر وكمله وتتبعه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that whatever Quranic interpretation he took came from ʿAlī.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: «ما أخذت من تفسير القرآن فعن علي بن أبي طالب»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r11.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r11.claim: ʿAlī praised Ibn ʿAbbās’s exegesis and encouraged people to learn from him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r11.anchor: وكان علي بن أبي طالب يثني على تفسير ابن عباس ويحث على الأخذ عنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r12.claim: Ibn Masʿūd calls Ibn ʿAbbās an excellent interpreter of the Quran.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r12.anchor: وكان عبد الله بن مسعود يقول: «نعم ترجمان القرآن عبد الله بن عباس»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r13.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r13.claim: The Prophet prayed that God grant Ibn ʿAbbās understanding in religion, a supplication the author says is sufficient testimony.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p41/r13.anchor: وهو الذي يقول فيه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «اللهم فقهه في الدين» وحسبك بهذه الدعوة

MUSLIM:403/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:403/r1.speaker: عائشة
MUSLIM:403/r1.claim: Aisha reports that true dreams began Muhammad's revelation, followed by solitary worship at Hira and Gabriel's three commands to read; Gabriel then gave the opening verses through 96:5.
MUSLIM:403/r1.anchor: أَنَّ عَائِشَةَ، زَوْجَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَخْبَرَتْهُ أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ كَانَ أَوَّلُ مَا بُدِئَ بِهِ

MUSLIM:403/r2.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:403/r2.speaker: author
MUSLIM:403/r2.claim: The report glosses taḥannuth in the cave as worship.
MUSLIM:403/r2.anchor: فكان يخلو بغار حراء يتحنث فيه - وهو التعبد - الليالي أولات العدد

MUSLIM:403/r3.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:403/r3.speaker: خديجة
MUSLIM:403/r3.claim: Khadija reassures Muhammad that God will never disgrace him, citing his care for kin, truthfulness, generosity, and aid to people in need.
MUSLIM:403/r3.anchor: قالت له خديجة كلا أبشر فوالله لا يخزيك الله أبدا والله إنك لتصل الرحم وتصدق الحديث وتحمل الكل وتكسب المعدوم وتقري الضيف

MUSLIM:403/r4.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:403/r4.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
MUSLIM:403/r4.claim: Waraqa identifies the visitor as the messenger sent to Moses, predicts Muhammad's people will expel and oppose him, and says he would support him if alive.
MUSLIM:403/r4.anchor: فقال له ورقة هذا الناموس الذي أنزل على موسى

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r2.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that true dreams began revelation, then the Prophet loved solitude, worshiped at Ḥirāʾ for several nights, and Khadīja supplied his provisions.
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r2.anchor: عن عائشة قالت : أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة في النوم

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r3.claim: ʿĀʾisha recounts Gabriel's three forceful embraces in the cave, Muhammad's repeated reply that he could not read, and Gabriel's recitation of the opening revelation; Muhammad returned trembling.
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r3.anchor: فجاءه الملك فيه فقال : اقرأ . قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r4.speaker: خديجة
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r4.claim: In ʿĀʾisha's report, Khadīja reassures Muhammad that God will never disgrace him, citing his kinship ties, truthfulness, bearing burdens, hospitality, and help in adversity.
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r4.anchor: يا خديجة ، ما لي : فأخبرها الخبر وقال : " قد خشيت علي " . فقالت له : كلا أبشر فوالله لا يخزيك الله أبدا ؛ إنك لتصل الرحم

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r5.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r5.claim: Waraqa ibn Nawfal, Khadīja's relative, was a pre-Islamic Christian who wrote Arabic and Gospel material in it; he identified the angel as the messenger sent to Moses, predicted opposition and expulsion, and promised support if alive.
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r5.anchor: فقال ورقة : هذا الناموس الذي أنزل على موسى

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr adds, with the qualifier “as has reached us,” that after Waraqa's death revelation paused and grief brought Muhammad repeatedly to mountain peaks, where Gabriel reassured him he was truly God's messenger.
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r6.anchor: وفَتَر الوحي فترة حتى حَزن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم - فيما بلغنا -

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r7.claim: Ibn Kathīr says the report is transmitted in both Ṣaḥīḥs through al-Zuhrī; he notes that he examined its chain, text, and meanings in his Bukhārī commentary.
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r7.anchor: وهذا الحديث مخرج في الصحيحين من حديث الزهري

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r8.claim: Ibn Kathīr says these opening verses are God's first mercy to humanity and His first blessing upon them.
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r8.anchor: وهُنَّ أول رحمة رَحم الله بها العباد

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r10.speaker: author

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r10.anchor: أن عَلّم الإنسان ما لم يعلم

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r13.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r13.claim: Another transmitted saying promises that whoever acts on what he knows will be granted knowledge he did not previously know.

MUSNAD-AHMAD:25959/r1.speaker: عائشة
MUSNAD-AHMAD:25959/r1.claim: Aisha reports clear dreams preceded Muhammad’s worship at Hira; Gabriel’s three squeezes led to reciting al-ʿAlaq 96:1–5. Khadija consoled him citing virtues; Waraqa identified Gabriel as Moses’s messenger and predicted opposition; after a reported pause, Gabriel reassured him.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:25959/r1.anchor: عن عائشة أنها قالت: " أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF:96:4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:4/r1.claim: Teaching people what they did not know shows God's complete generosity and moves them from the darkness of ignorance to the light of knowledge.
KASHSHAF:96:4/r1.anchor: فدلّ على كمال كرمه بأنه علم عباده ما لم يعلموا ،   ونقلهم من ظلمة الجهل إلى نور العلم

KASHSHAF:96:5/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:5/r1.speaker: author
