KASHSHAF:96:5/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:5/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:5/r2.claim: Writing preserves sciences, wisdom, earlier peoples' reports and sayings, and revealed books; without it, religion and worldly affairs could not be properly sustained.
KASHSHAF:96:5/r2.anchor: وما دوّنت العلوم ،   ولا قيدت الحكم ،   ولا ضبطت أخبار الأولين ومقالاتهم

KASHSHAF:96:5/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:5/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:5/r3.claim: The pen and script are by themselves enough to demonstrate God's precise wisdom and subtle governance.
KASHSHAF:96:5/r3.anchor: ولو لم يكن على دقيق حكمة الله ولطيف تدبيره ودليل إلا أمر القلم والخط ،   لكفى به

KASHSHAF:96:5/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:5/r4.speaker: ابن الزبير
KASHSHAF:96:5/r4.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr's reading specifies that God taught writing with the pen.

MAWARDI:96:5/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:5/r1.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
MAWARDI:96:5/r1.claim: Qatāda and Ibn Zayd take what God taught as writing with the pen.
MAWARDI:96:5/r1.anchor: أحدهما : الخط بالقلم ،   قاله قتادة وابن زيد

MAWARDI:96:5/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:5/r2.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI:96:5/r2.claim: Ibn Shajara interprets it as teaching every craft a person learns.
MAWARDI:96:5/r2.anchor: الثاني : علمه كل صنعة علمها فتعلم ،   قاله ابن شجرة

MAWARDI:96:5/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:5/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:5/r3.claim: Māwardī also suggests that God taught the human, through the initial state of creation, evidence of how He created him and could later move him according to His will.
MAWARDI:96:5/r3.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثاً : علمه من حاله في ابتداء خلقه ما يستدل به على خلقه ،   وأن ينقله من بعد على إرادته

NASAFI:96:5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:5/r1.claim: God's complete generosity appears in teaching people what they did not know and moving them from the darkness of ignorance to the light of knowledge.
NASAFI:96:5/r1.anchor: فدل على كمال كرمه بأنه علم عباده ما لم يعلموا

NASAFI:96:5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:5/r2.claim: Writing has immense benefits: it records sciences and wisdom, preserves earlier reports and revealed books, and is indispensable to religious and worldly affairs; the pen and script alone show God's subtle wisdom.
NASAFI:96:5/r2.anchor: ونبه على فضل علم الكتابة لما فيه من المنافع العظيمة

QURTUBI:96:5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:5/r1.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:96:5/r1.claim: One view identifies the human taught as Adam, whom God taught the names of everything in every language, as in 2:31.
QURTUBI:96:5/r1.anchor: قيل : " الإنسان " هنا آدم عليه السلام . علمه أسماء كل شيء

QURTUBI:96:5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:5/r2.claim: Adam named what he had been taught before the angels, demonstrating his rank and prophethood, establishing God's proof, and leading the angels to obey when they witnessed God's power and command.
QURTUBI:96:5/r2.anchor: وذكره آدم للملائكة كما علمه . وبذلك ظهر فضله ، وتبين قدره

QURTUBI:96:5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:5/r3.claim: Adam's descendants inherited and transmitted this knowledge from generation to generation and people to people.
QURTUBI:96:5/r3.anchor: ثم توارثت ذلك ذريته خلفا بعد سلف ، وتناقلوه قوما عن قوم .

QURTUBI:96:5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:5/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:96:5/r4.claim: Another view identifies the human as Muhammad, citing God's statement that He taught him what he did not know; on this view the teaching is future because this was among the earliest revelations.
QURTUBI:96:5/r4.anchor: وقيل : " الإنسان " هنا الرسول محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم . دليله قوله تعالى

QURTUBI:96:5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:5/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:96:5/r5.claim: A general interpretation takes human to mean humanity, since people emerge from their mothers knowing nothing.
QURTUBI:96:5/r5.anchor: وقيل : هو عام لقوله تعالى : " والله أخرجكم من بطون أمهاتكم

RAZI:96:5/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:5/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:96:5/r1.claim: The clause may add that God taught humanity by the pen and also taught other things, with no conjunction; Rāzī compares successive clauses such as honoring, helping, and granting wealth.
RAZI:96:5/r1.anchor: علمه بالقلم وعلمه أيضا غير ذلك

RAZI:96:5/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:5/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:96:5/r2.claim: Alternatively, the two teaching clauses have one meaning: God taught humanity by the pen what it did not know, and the second explains the first.
